claim: For every nondegenerate Euclidean isosceles triangle \(ABC\), if \(m_a,m_b,m_c\) are the medians, \(h_a,h_b,h_c\) the altitudes, \(s\) the semiperimeter, and \(r\) the inradius, then \[m_a+m_b+m_c-(h_a+h_b+h_c)\ge s-3\sqrt{3}\,r.\] Equality holds if and only if the triangle is equilateral. Thus Liu's 2012 Conjecture 4 holds on the full isosceles subclass.

integrity.equality_scope: equilateral triangle only within the isosceles family
integrity.finite_computation_role: certificate replay of symbolic identities only, not evidence by sampling
integrity.proof_type: analytic exact one-variable reduction with exact algebraic certificate

scientific_limitations: The theorem proves Liu's 2012 Conjecture 4 only for nondegenerate isosceles Euclidean triangles; scalene triangles remain outside the claim. Originality is relative to the explicitly checked literature and searches.
title: Liu's median-altitude conjecture for isosceles triangles
